root_motivation: **Who:** an autonomous agent about to deploy, send, spend or delete something its user should approve while the user is away from the chat. **What:** ask once, hand over a link, block, act on the answer; never hang and never guess. **Why not today:** the only long-poll is host.msg.wait on an inbox a human cannot write to; the wait ceiling is prose in a descriptor and two clamp literals; composing a blocking question from a url-shared tool costs three host calls. **Consequence:** approvals are skipped or guessed.
user_persona: An agent that calls host.ask.create, sends its user the url, and loops host.ask.wait until answered or expired; the user who taps a button on a phone with no login; Operator Joe reading host.ask.list.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a 0.106.0-shaped test host, When a test composes the blocking question from `host.tool_share(visibility="url")` on an `answer` tool plus `host.msg.wait`, and then runs `host.ask.create` + `host.ask.wait`, Then it records both call counts and end-to-end latencies in the test output, and the verb path uses strictly fewer host calls (the PRD is parked if not).

Given `host.ask.create` with 2 options, When the URL is fetched with no key and one option is POSTed, Then the agent's blocked `host.ask.wait` returns `status: answered` with that choice within 2 s, and a second POST returns 409 `ask_answered` naming the first choice.

Given `WAIT_MAX_S`, When the `host.msg.wait` descriptor, the `host.ask.wait` descriptor and `host.quickstart.limits.wait_max_s` are rendered, Then all three carry the constant's value and `rg 'clamp\(1, 25\)' src` returns no lines.
Given an ask with `ttl_s: 2`, When `host.ask.wait` is called 3 s later, Then it returns error `ask_expired` with `next_call: host.ask.create`, and the page returns the 404 bytes.
Given a key-less `host.ask.wait` on bare `/mcp`, When it is called, Then it returns `tenant_key_missing` in under 1 s and no tenant row is created.
Given a free tenant with 5 pending asks, When `host.ask.create` runs, Then it fails `asks_limit`, and `host.quickstart.limits.plan.asks_open_max` reads 5 from `plans.rs`.
Given two concurrent POSTs of different choices to one ask, When both complete, Then exactly one is recorded, the other is 409, and `host.ask.get` shows one `answered` event.

Given prod after deploy, When the help page and the plan page are fetched, Then both reflect the new registry entries (Live; evidence: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://mcphost.dev/help/ask_expired` prints 200 and `curl -s https://mcphost.dev/plans.json | grep -c asks_open_max` prints 1 or more)
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred -- operator-provisioned: needs prod after deploy (help page and plans.json fetched from https://mcphost.dev).

scope: src/asks.rs (new): host.ask.create/wait/get/list, WAIT_MAX_S, signed /a/{id} page (GET render, POST first-answer-wins), per-ask Notify with a 1 s re-read, 30-day retention prune.
migrations/0083_asks.sql + src/db.rs: asks and ask_events tables; Db::with_conn is pub(crate).

src/handler.rs, src/messaging.rs, src/runs.rs, src/control.rs: ask tool descriptors and dispatch, the two wait clamps and three descriptors rendered from WAIT_MAX_S, limits.wait_max_s, NEVER_SIGNS_UP arm guard.

src/plans.rs: asks_open_max (free 5, pro 100). src/errors.rs, src/help.rs: ask_expired, ask_answered, choice_invalid, asks_limit. src/chart.rs: shared sign_path. src/http.rs: /a/{id} route. src/paged.rs: host.ask.list unpaged reason.
non_goals: Free-text answers; delivering the link to a channel (host.notify.send); multi-user votes; rendering agent threads; an inbox message on answer (open question, not built).

additional.notify_registry: The per-ask Notify registry is process-wide (a OnceLock map keyed by ask id), not an AppState field, so no AppState literal in the crate or its tests changes.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can an agent not ask its user a blocking question in one verb pair?
five_whys_trace.a: host.msg.wait reads an inbox only keyed agents can write to, so a human has no way to answer.

five_whys_trace.q: Why not compose it from a url-shared tool?
five_whys_trace.a: That costs publish + share + wait (3 host calls) against create + wait (2), measured by AC1.
The 25 s ceiling was two clamp literals and prose; a derived constant cannot drift from the descriptors or quickstart limits.

ambiguities_resolved.question: next_call shape?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: A tool-name string (next_call) plus an args object (next_args), so the literal AC text next_call == host.ask.create holds and the call stays executable.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Where does the wait wake-up registry live?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Process-wide OnceLock map in asks.rs; the PRD's AppState placement would have touched every AppState literal.
